From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form review — mapping source of loss (direct vs consequential)

Samantha — attaching an updated MSA redline and a short memo mapping the typical loss categories we see to contract language. Key ask: can your legal team confirm which of the Acme-specific damages examples (lost revenue from service outage; permanent loss of telemetry; reputational harm) you want carved out as consequential vs direct?

Highlights from our side:
- We can accept a focused carve-out for direct losses caused by data deletion where we have committed backup guarantees (Order Form §5).
- We push back on broad lost-profits carve-outs that would effectively negate the cap. We propose a defined list of recoverable direct losses (repair costs, reprocessing fees, documented third-party fees).
- For goodwill/reputation, suggest express exclusion unless there is demonstrable, measurable revenue loss tied to an Acme billing metric.

Attached: Acme_MSA_Redline_v3.docx (redline with inline comments) and OrderForm_Acme_20270815.pdf (service commitments).

Next steps: if you can indicate line items to accept/reject by Wednesday (8/25), we can circulate final language for signature.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Sales Counsel | Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks, we reviewed the first draft. Main points from Acme legal:
- We need broader protections for lost profits tied to outages that impact our subscription metrics (MAU, billing events).
- Data-loss carve-outs: Acme expects indemnity for permanent loss of customer telemetry only when caused by gross negligence or willful misconduct, not routine outages.
- Reputation/goodwill: want to preserve recovery for brand damage where we can show downstream revenue impact.

Can your team propose concrete language that maps examples to the MSA sections (cap calculation, excluded damages, consequential exceptions)?

Samantha
VP, Partnerships | Acme Cloud

-----Original Message-----
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form review — mapping source of loss (direct vs consequential)

Samantha — thanks for the quick read. I’ve pulled the suggested clauses into the redline and added a short mapping table in the margin (doc page 4). Two practical proposals that should help narrow negotiation:

1) Defined "Recoverable Direct Losses" (proposed new §9.2):
- out-of-pocket costs to restore customer data that Redwood caused by its software or operational error (requires documented estimate from an approved vendor);
- reprocessing costs for lost data where re-ingestion is feasible and agreed timelines are met;
- fees paid to third-party idempotent services required to remediate the error.

2) Limit on Consequential Damages (proposed §9.3):
- Broad bar on consequential damages, with carve-outs for: (a) claims for bodily injury or death; (b) direct damages arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; and (c) explicit, pre-approved lost-revenue categories listed in the Order Form (e.g., chargeback refunds tied to billing mismatch). Any lost-profits request outside of the Order Form categories requires prior written approval and a different commercial bucket.

3) Goodwill/reputation approach — practical test suggestion:
- Allow recovery for reputational harm only if Acme provides contemporaneous metrics that show a measurable revenue delta (e.g., 25% month-over-month drop in billable events for two consecutive billing periods) and links the drop to a Redwood incident via agreed post-incident analysis.

I’ve highlighted each change in the redline by color and added a short rationale. We’re flexible on narrowing the Order Form categories to those your GTM team can commit to measuring. If legal wants to propose specific revenue metrics, we can treat that as an Order Form annex rather than changing the MSA cap.

Can Laura coordinate an internal quick review with contract ops on the measurement thresholds?

Thanks,
Jonas
Sr. Sales Counsel | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Acme_MSA_Redline_v3.docx (mapping table on pg4)]

Samantha/Tom — looping in our Contract Ops and Product teams on the measurement ask. Quick summary from our internal review:

- We can accept a narrowly tailored lost-profits path tied to explicit billing metrics, but only if those metrics are captured in the Order Form annex and the measurement methodology is mutually agreed.
- For permanent loss of telemetry, Redwood will accept direct damages where we have failed to meet an explicit backup RTO/RPO in the Order Form.
- We cannot accept open-ended recovery for goodwill/reputation without the measurable-metric gating described below.

Proposed timeline:
- Wed 8/25: Acme legal to mark which Order Form categories they want included for lost-profits consideration (quick checkboxes on the shared Drive doc).
- Thu 8/26: Redwood product to produce a short "measurement spec" doc (link below) that defines how the billing events/MAU are calculated and what logs are authoritative.
- Fri 8/27: Final redline exchange and if both sides agree, move to signature over the following week.
